quality.location: app/src/main.ts (rollOffset initialization); legacy continuation path not supplied
quality.description: The global offset default changes to 0 while legacy continuation keeps the 80 lb source payload. The packet shows no code that restores the former -0.109375 command, so a continued legacy flight may switch to payload-without-correction. The diagnosis says these two corrections belong together. Expected: a continued legacy flight applies a deliberate, disclosed offset policy, with a test. Reproduction: continue a legacy recording with no loading group through the app, then compare its aileron command and bank trend with the recording.
quality.evidence: main.ts hunk sets `let rollOffset = 0`. The diagnostics report source loading at zero aileron reaching +35.303° at 7 s and the 100 m floor before 30 s, and say removing the correction alone is insufficient. The worker harness does not exercise the app's offset.

quality.description: The missing-loading continuation case cannot distinguish the native source fallback from configuration retained from the previous init, because the preceding flight also carried the source external mass. R-SIM-11 forbids using the current custom load here. The native harness configures once and then calls `_gf_init` repeatedly, which suggests configuration may persist across native inits, although the worker's module lifecycle is not supplied. Expected: start a zero-external or custom flight, immediately resume the no-loading state in the same worker, and assert the full source-default loading group.
quality.evidence: The worker harness runs `loading: DEFAULT_LOADING`, then `resume_state: legacy`, then `resume_state: noLoading`, and asserts only `payload_external_kg` and step. `initialize()` in the native harness shows one `_gf_configure_loading` call before six `_gf_init` calls.

quality.description: The diagnostics say the declaration exports `FLIGHT_DEFAULT_LOADING`, and the panel now imports that symbol, but the code diff has no `loading.d.ts` hunk. If the declaration is not part of the revision, TypeScript checking of `loading-panel.ts` would fail. A successful bundle or test run does not prove otherwise. Expected: the reviewed diff includes the declaration and the validation record includes a type-check result.
quality.evidence: The artifact table lists `studies/e1-browser/sim/loading.d.ts` with a local hash. The code diff contains `loading.js` but not `loading.d.ts`, and the Validation section lists no type-check.

quality.description: The native script is presented as a regression but asserts no behavior beyond finite telemetry, CAS matching, native call return codes and exact repeatability. Restoring the old payload or offset, or a new 70/90 kt trim failure, would still pass, even though the diagnosis relies on successful 90 kt trim. Expected: assert the trim status per declared case and add pre-declared comparison criteria, or label the script as diagnostic only and not as passing regression evidence.
quality.evidence: `trimStatus` is stored but never asserted. The only behavioral assertions are the CAS convergence check and the repeat digest/final-state comparison. The Validation section reports the 48 cases as passing.

quality.description: The case matrix has no independent rudder pulse. Rudder is only ever `-pulse`, coupled to an aileron pulse. Pulses are also positive only and run only at trim power, so independent yaw response and left/right asymmetry are unmeasured even though the model is laterally asymmetric and retains actuator hysteresis. Expected: add rudder-only and opposite-sign pulses at the declared speeds and powers.
quality.evidence: The configs loop uses `pulse_norm` of `.1` and `.45` with `link` true or false and `power: 'trim'`. In `run()`, `const rudder = config.link ? -pulse : 0`.

quality.description: The app-level changes have no identifiable test in the diff: zero initial roll offset and slider state, the loading panel's normal draft, the external-station label, and the renamed legacy offset button. Worker initialization asserts zero aileron but does not cover the main-thread offset. Expected: named app or browser assertions for each behavior.
quality.evidence: The only app test hunk is `control-settings.test.ts`. The Validation section says `actualbrowser6groups pass` but does not name the groups or assertions.

quality.description: The new default applies to every non-resume init that omits `loading`, not only to app flights. Callers relying on the old implicit source payload silently change mass and digests, and a native engine without `_gf_configure_loading` now fails where a no-loading init previously skipped configuration. Expected: inventory omitted-loading callers and pin explicit `DEFAULT_LOADING` wherever historical behavior is intended.
quality.evidence: worker.js hunk: `resume?loadingFromState(resume):(msg.loading??FLIGHT_DEFAULT_LOADING)`, followed by the existing `_gf_configure_loading` guard. No caller inventory is supplied.

quality.description: The new note drops the statement that manual rudder takes priority. With the link enabled, saying Q/W controls rudder independently does not explain that nonzero manual rudder overrides the link. It also no longer says plainly that bank input drives the nosewheel. Expected: state the bank-to-rudder/nosewheel link and the manual override.
quality.evidence: The diff replaces `Bank input also steers rudder and nosewheel. Q/W takes priority.` The R-INPUT-1 text requires that nonzero manual rudder overrides.

quality.description: The comment still describes the variable as the E1 fixture's empirical offset, but it now holds a neutral default of 0. Expected: describe it as an optional experimental offset that starts at zero.

`native_binary_not_rebuilt: true` is hard-coded rather than measured, so the artifact can assert it even if the binary was rebuilt. The report also omits the `loading.js` hash that the worker report includes. Expected: remove the constant or derive it from pinned expected hashes, and record the `loading.js` hash.

quality.description: The state probe sends a KAP140 `baro` command, so reading state goes through an autopilot command path before the state later used for continuation is captured. Expected: use a read-only state request, or show that this command cannot affect the compared state.
quality.evidence: `const state = () => send({ type: 'kap140', command: { action: 'baro' } }, 'state')`, then `legacy = await state()` before resume.

limitations: This review used only the frozen packet. I ran no checks, and all runtime results are the packet's reported evidence.
Generated artifacts and local hashes could not be inspected or matched to file contents.

Full source is not supplied for `main.ts`, `worker.js`, `loading.js`, the settings and loading panels, or the continuation and trace paths. Findings about those paths are limited to the diff and stated as evidence gaps where behavior is not shown.
The executing WASM has a hash that differs from its build record, so results apply to the identified bytes and not to verified pinned source.

The packet reports bank and roll measurements but no oscillation metric or sensitivity change. It shows the reported sensitivity and oscillation are not fully resolved, and hands-off drift remains (+15.241° at 30 s, no external mass, 90 kt trim power).
CLI routing and returned model names are evidence, not backend attestation.
Packet review does not independently execute the packet's test commands.
